name: John Cabot to Newfoundland
summary: A Venetian sailing for Henry VII crosses the North Atlantic in the small Matthew and lands on a coast he takes for north-east Asia, five centuries after the Norse. The cod he reports, so thick 'they could be taken with baskets', draws fishermen for centuries. He vanishes on a second voyage in 1498.

stops.note: The Matthew sails with about 18 men.
The last land before the crossing.
Landfall: Cabot plants the banners of England and Venice.
Seas so full of cod they could be taken with baskets.
Home in 15 days; Henry VII gives him £10.
